newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open mostly unchanged Friday, with prices seen steady ahead of CFTC's Commitments of Traders Report due out after today's close, dealers said.
Thursday, July ended 0.10 cent lower at 11.41 cents a lb after trading from 11.46 cents to 11.33 cents. October settled down 0.11 at 11.21 cents, with the rest 0.11 to 0.05 weaker.

Mixed selling pressured prices early yesterday while producer buying held the market steady through the close, floor sources said. The market is expected to hold its current range until next week, when the speculators are seen liquidating a substantial net long position.
An estimated 33,315 lots changed hands on the day.
Russia will buy 3.25 million tonnes of Cuban raw sugar in 1997, in exchange for crude oil. Under the agreement, reported today in the Russian press, suppliers would be selected through a tender.
Technical support was seen from 11.20 to 11.00 cents.

In London, white sugar futures eased slightly on Friday in thin dealings. At 0838 EDT/1238 GMT, LIFFE spot August contract was down $0.40 at $326.30, and the rest of the board stood $0.10 lower to $0.10 firmer.
